doc.title: Young Snooky — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Sessions with Johnny Hodges and George Benson
summary: Young does not remember a Johnny Hodges session and only vaguely recalls recording with George Benson before he was famous.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: So we‘ll do that later. But, I want to talk to you about some of your recordings, because you recorded with so many people, I just wanted to, even if you don‘t remember exactly what happened in the studio, but let‘s talk about playing in Johnny Hodges band.
Johnny Hodges, Rabbit, Johnny Hodges from Duke. Yeah, talk about that. You recorded with him.
You know, I don‘t remember recording with Johnny Hodges.
There‘s a piece that‘s called ―Don‘t Sleep in the Subway.‖
Well, [laughs] that might be a tough one. Okay, how about George Benson?
I did. I remember the name when he was just, what year was that?
It doesn‘t say, but he wasn‘t really up there yet, you know, when I recorded with him, you know what I‘m saying, he hadn‘t gotten to be a big man yet like he is now.
